chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Humayri narrated from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Yazid ibn Ishaq, from al-Hasan ibn Atiyyah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The noble characteristics are ten. If you can, let them be in you. For they may exist in a man but not in his son, and they may exist in his son but not in his father, and they may exist in a slave but not in a free person. They are: courage in battle, honesty in speech, fulfilling trusts, maintaining kinship ties, honoring the guest, feeding the beggar, repaying favors, showing humility to the neighbor, showing humility to the companion, and their head (or essence) is modesty.
ai.seo_question: What are the ten noble characteristics (makarim) in Shia hadith and what is their foundation?
ai.summary: In *Al-Khisal*, Shaykh al-Saduq records this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to emphasize that moral nobility (*al-makarim*) is an individual spiritual achievement rather than an inherited genetic trait, as it may reside in a person but not their father or son. The enumeration highlights ten key virtues, culminating in modesty (*al-haya'*) as the 'head' or foundation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on internal character over external social hierarchy.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 10-11 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abdullah ibn Ja’far al-Homayry quoted Yazid ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Atiye that Aba Abdullahas-Sadiq (MGB) said, “

The following ten characteristics are due to nobility. Try to attain them if you can. They may exist in a father, but not exist in his son. They may exist in a son but not exist in his father. They may exist in a slave, but not in a free person. They are: courage in a battle; honesty in speech; returning what you are entrusted with; visiting the relations of kin; entertaining the guests; feeding the beggars; returning favors; respecting and being kind to neighbors; respecting and being kind to friends; and above all being modest.”
